called for a statement name that is no built-in: looks for an NSS function of that name (objects of type 8), binds the arguments, switches to it; an unknown name is skipped, so Waitkey and XBOX360_* calls do nothing
true if a string holds only digits, + and -
true if the text starts a value: a digit, $, #, (, +, -, or Message( Conquest( Array( AssocArray( VariableValue( ...
( or [ starts a parenthesised expression, anything else goes to eval_primary
expression evaluator, values: the 31 value built-ins (Random, String, Count, Conquest, ...; research/nitroplus/evalnames.py), MessageBox styles, SYSTEM_ variables
SetVolume: fills a command record (object name, time, volume string, tempo) and applies sound_set_volume_cb to every object the name matches
resolves an object name in a command record (@alias, a/b paths, * wildcards) and calls the record callback on each match
SetVolume callback per object: calls sound_set_volume with the record time
compares an argument with SCREEN, VIDEO, SCENE (CreateTexture sources, unverified)

volume string (0-1000, or @n relative to the current volume) clamped to 0-1000; time 0: set now, else start sound_volume_fade_thread. DirectSound volume = max(-10000, 3322*log10(f*v/1000)), f = the float at +0x118 (probably the volume setting), 0 = -10000; reaching 0 stops a playing sound
stops a sound (IDirectSoundBuffer::Stop) and resets its state
linear volume ramp from the current to the target volume over the given time, in 50 ms steps; at the end the same 0-stops rule as sound_set_volume
assigns a $SYSTEM_ variable: compares the name with 62 setting names built on the stack (sound_volume_bgm, ...)
MSVC CRT log10 on ST0 (fldlg2/fyl2x)
256-byte substitution table for NPA names and data (file offset 0x134830; research/nitroplus/npa.py)
